name: fii_dii_flow_signal_v1
author: claude-4.6-opus-agent-4
thesis: Foreign Institutional Investor (FII) and Domestic Institutional Investor (DII) net buy/sell data is published by NSE with a T+0 lag (provisional data by 17:00 IST for same-day activity). However, intraday proxies for institutional flow can be estimated from order size distribution: large orders (>₹10L notional) are predominantly institutional. By tracking the ratio of large orders to total orders in real-time, we infer whether institutions are net buying or selling. When large-order flow diverges from small-order flow (institutions buying while retail selling), the institutional direction tends to dominate over the next 30-60 minutes. The inefficiency exists because order-level data analysis requires infrastructure beyond most retail setups.
stock_filter: ADV(20) > ₹100 Cr; F&O listed (institutional participation higher in F&O stocks)

indicators.name: Large_Order_NetBuy
indicators.params: sum(trade_value * sign(trade_side) for trades with value > ₹10L) over last 30 bars

indicators.name: Small_Order_NetBuy
indicators.params: sum(trade_value * sign(trade_side) for trades with value < ₹1L) over last 30 bars

indicators.name: Prev_Day_FII_Flow
indicators.params: sign(FII_net_buy) from previous day's provisional data

conditions: Flow_Divergence > 0 (institutions buying while retail selling — smart money divergence)
Prev_Day_FII_Flow > 0 (FII were net buyers yesterday — momentum in institutional flows)
close >= vwap (price above VWAP confirming institutional buying pressure)

exit.trailing_stop: After 25 bps profit, trail at 15 bps from high-water mark
exit.signal_exit: Institutional_Pressure crosses zero (institutional flow direction reverses)

risk.position_sizing: Fixed ₹1L; increase to ₹1.25L if Institutional_Pressure > 0.5 and Prev_Day_FII_Flow agrees

filters.vix_filter: India VIX < 25; during high VIX, institutional flows can be erratic (forced selling by leveraged FIIs)
filters.time_filter: No entries before 09:30 (need 30 bars for flow accumulation) or after 15:10
filters.volume_filter: At least 20 large orders (>₹10L) in last 30 bars (sufficient institutional activity to be meaningful)
filters.trend_filter: NIFTY 50 direction should agree with institutional flow direction
filters.event_filter: Avoid F&O expiry days (institutional hedging activity distorts flow signals)
other_filters: FII/DII data must be available from previous day; skip on first trading day after a holiday

edge.edge_decay_risk: Low-Medium — order-level flow analysis requires trade-by-trade data access and real-time processing; the ₹10L threshold for 'large orders' is a reasonable but imperfect proxy for institutional activity

weaknesses: The ₹10L threshold for 'large orders' is arbitrary — wealthy retail traders may place orders above ₹10L, and institutions may use algorithmic slicing to place many small orders, contaminating both categories
Trade-by-trade data is not available on all retail platforms (Zerodha does not provide order-level data) — this strategy requires a data vendor or exchange membership for real-time trade data
Previous day FII/DII data is backward-looking and FII flows can reverse sharply (e.g., RBI policy surprise) — using yesterday's flow to predict today's direction assumes continuity that may not exist
prior_art: FII/DII flow analysis is common in Indian financial media; Sias (2004) on institutional herding; Brunnermeier & Pedersen (2009) on smart money; order flow analysis in Easley & O'Hara (1987); Kyle (1985) on informed trading
notes: Consider using Zerodha Kite's market depth data as a partial proxy for order flow — while it's not trade-by-trade, the bid/ask quantity imbalance at multiple levels can indicate institutional presence. Alternatively, use NSE's tick-by-tick data feed if available.
